evidence_policy: Executable source, executable configuration, existing tests and observed runtime only; prose comments/docstrings are not behavioral authority. New measured results belong in separate reports.

rows.scope: Legacy ParamSpace and MSQ initialization for identical domains and requested candidate count k
rows.code_delta: ParamSpace now validates every supplied choice through the shared canonical execution identity and rejects collisions. Requested candidates are still materialized; Grid construction is byte-identical.
rows.performance_implication: Choice admission adds work proportional to the supplied choices and their serialized size. Legacy candidate columns still retain O(k*d) values; Grid initially retains dimensions without expanding the Cartesian product.
rows.limitation: No parameter construction latency or memory scaling rerun is prescribed. Added identity validation is meaningful work, not a demonstrated regression.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

rows.scope: Legacy generate and MSQ Grid/Random/Sobol accepted-candidate streams
rows.code_delta: Grid, Random and Sobol implementations are byte-identical. SearchStrategy delegates to the same canonical execution hash. Legacy generate still filters the remaining frame after each draw.
rows.performance_implication: Consuming a legacy k-row frame still repeatedly scans shrinking frames, approximately quadratic total row-position work. MSQ accepted-hash retention and bounded Random/Sobol retries remain.
rows.limitation: No enumeration throughput or search-distribution measurement. Domain identity admission should not be represented as a faster enumerator.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

rows.scope: Fresh process through one admitted output, plus first full-wrapper call separately
rows.code_delta: The frozen zero-cost snapshot adapter remains signature-compatible. New optional class mapping and explicit-exit support do not activate in this replay.
rows.performance_implication: Old and latest must be measured on the same host with identical dependencies. Process-launch-to-first-valid includes source verification, imports, data, oracle and validation; first API call is a different boundary.
rows.limitation: No October19-to-October29 timing ratio. The separate kernel diagnostic first call follows all full-wrapper calls and is not process-cold.
rows.measurement_state: Measured only for the matched finite snapshot replay; fresh process boundaries include harness verification and oracle work.

rows.scope: Recorded-data split/model/search/recording contract through durable successful rounds
rows.code_delta: Round validation, holdout composition, error handling, and additional recorded evidence have expanded. Per-round result CSV appends and buffered logging remain in the serial/MSQ execution paths.
rows.performance_implication: Richer evidence and admission can change end-to-end cost. The unchanged native 48-round factorized harness can measure its exact workload; it cannot establish general research throughput.
rows.limitation: One fresh-versus-reuse pair per revision is a mechanism check, not a repeated latency experiment. No model equivalence or broad scaling claim follows from snapshot replay.
rows.measurement_state: One 48-round native fitted-preparation pair per revision; general campaign-throughput status remains Unknown.

rows.scope: Eligible deterministic serial snapshot Grid workloads using factorize=True
rows.code_delta: New explicit stage reuse contracts, native declarations and domain projections broaden admissible signal reuse. Fitted-preparation reuse still has narrower RobustScaler/NextReturn/QuantileBinary/window-return/lag-range admission. Cache hits now compose holdout proofs and replay warnings.
rows.performance_implication: Domain projections can avoid unnecessary Cartesian validation, but custom full-parameter dependencies can still enlarge admission work. Supported factorized paths retain fitted artifacts and signals to avoid repeated fits; bounded entry counts are not byte budgets.
rows.limitation: Folds, allocation, objectives, event execution and explicit exits remain outside factorization admission. Only the unchanged recorded-data harness is scheduled to quantify reuse; verify 48 rows, 24 model fits per arm, target/scaler 24 versus 1, and equal 12-decimal outputs within each revision.
rows.measurement_state: Both revisions: target/scaler fits 24→1, model fits 24 per arm, 48 rounds per arm, all four scientific digests equal at 12 decimals. One descriptive timing pair per revision.

rows.scope: Aligned indicator/feature outputs, including causal quantile-line columns and FFD admission
rows.code_delta: EMA and shared line-array computation are byte-identical. SMA/CCI gain argument validation; stochastic wrapping now supports lazy expressions. Positive-quantile end-event columns use expanding completed-line thresholds. FFD gains finite-input/recurrence checks.
rows.performance_implication: The causal quantile path maintains heaps per direction and scans recent completed events per row. This fixes the information set and changes the work; timing it against the old whole-frame threshold is not equal-semantics optimization. Quantile zero retains the vectorized window-sum path.
rows.limitation: No adapted indicator timing is scheduled: the existing hardcoded-data benchmark is not independently matched here. The research-only active-span column still uses whole-frame selection. FFD has no new arbitrary maximum-weight or runtime quota.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

rows.scope: Zero-cost close-to-next-close all-in long/flat buy_and_hold and sma_cross on the same recorded 1h fixture
rows.code_delta: The long-flat return kernel and snapshot-ledger module are byte-identical. The wrapper adds optional explicit-exit behavior; the common adapter uses the unchanged default route.
rows.performance_implication: The frozen external contract, oracle, adapter and extraction can be reused byte-for-byte with two explicit source-catalog overlays. Precomputed targets, complete equity/held/fill parity, and post-call thread gates remain mandatory.
rows.limitation: Common results do not expose independent native cash/units/fee-ledger fields for Limen; fills are reconstructed from native position segments. Costed common replay remains unsupported by this adapter, and event execution is a separate contract.
rows.measurement_state: Five fresh measured processes per revision/strategy, nine warm calls per process, both strategies fully admitted. Aggregate ratios 0.905470/0.958419; observed ranges overlap, no algorithmic speedup attribution.

rows.scope: Account events and both-side forward trade labels under funding/timer policies
rows.code_delta: Event-plan construction can bypass the global key/cache for single-use candidates. TradeOutcomeTarget caches the accrual-presence decision, shares a full plan for no-accrual cases, reuses the immediate long/short candidate plan for accrual cases, disables state retention, and reads episodes directly.
rows.performance_implication: This removes repeated cache-key/ledger/state work from inspected target paths. The event cache remains limited by plan count and source-event count; these limits do not bound emitted timer states.
rows.limitation: No event-label throughput or scaling timing is scheduled. Long horizons can still revisit long suffixes. The improvement is code-inferred work avoidance, not a measured speedup.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

rows.scope: Sources, model/preparation caches, worker duplication, IPC and recorded outputs
rows.code_delta: Parallel workers now load a parent-written, hashed, read-only file snapshot of each source frame. Each worker reads bytes and deserializes its own DataFrame. Computation-cache accounting is byte-identical; factorized caches remain entry bounded.
rows.performance_implication: Source admission is stronger and the parent serializes once, but this is not memory mapping or shared DataFrame storage. Per-worker data/model copies and temporary serialization remain possible.
rows.limitation: Paired snapshot and native harness RSS is process-lifetime high-water, not incremental allocation, PSS, process-tree memory or a hard bound. No memory-scaling campaign is scheduled.
rows.measurement_state: Process-lifetime high-water RSS observed for finite single-process workloads; no process-tree, allocation-only or scaling measurement.

rows.scope: Admitted compiled CPU round execution with bounded queued work and deterministic ordered commits
rows.code_delta: Worker admission no longer uses only the old exact MLManifest/logreg/LightGBM whitelist; it reconstructs compiled shapes and checks resolved CPU/native-thread settings. Source snapshots, holdout authority and fold-promotion context enter initialization.
rows.performance_implication: More admitted compiled workloads can execute in workers. Pending work remains bounded, and commits still await pending[0] with checkpoint/feedback barriers, so head-of-line blocking remains.
rows.limitation: No parallel timing is newly introduced: the old parallel harness was inspected rather than measured in the original baseline. Native suite results can test correctness but do not establish scaling speedups.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

rows.criterion: Cache key, hit and eviction costs
rows.scope: Computation, fitted-preparation, prediction and event-plan cache boundaries
rows.code_delta: The computation-cache implementation is byte-identical. Prepared/signal cache paths now validate protected source/population/history evidence and refresh recency; unprotected operation has a cheaper binding path. Single-use event plans may opt out of key/cache work.
rows.performance_implication: Computation hits still require source scans/byte-key construction and cloned/copied outputs. Added evidence checks are real cache-hit work; reuse does not imply a zero-cost hit.
rows.limitation: No isolated hit/miss/eviction benchmark is scheduled. The factorized harness measures one admitted workload only, and entry bounds do not establish worst-case memory.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

rows.scope: Recorded terminal prefixes and interrupted serial/parallel recovery
rows.code_delta: Round-storage serialization/compression/dedup code is unchanged apart from an internal frames rename. Recovery now checks applicable evidence, typed parameters and richer holdout/exit/fold outputs. Checkpoints accept a committed state snapshot without rewinding the live sampler.
rows.performance_implication: Recovery correctness work has expanded. Full-prefix validation and serial CSV truncation/rewrite remain; dedup still serializes and hashes before determining that a frame blob is already present.
rows.limitation: No interrupted-campaign latency or output-size scaling measurement is scheduled. Stronger recovery validation should not be mistaken for a demonstrated runtime bound.
rows.measurement_state: Code delta inspected; no new criterion-specific timing or scaling claim.

cohort_policy: Only Limen rerun; original cohort catalog and historical evidence remain untouched.
